recognize_zh: 兩顆小至中型單核白血球（形似淋巴球）的細胞質內有粗大、深紫紅色顆粒，下方細胞顆粒尤其明顯且散布於核周與細胞質邊緣，符合 Alder-Reilly 異常（常見於黏多醣症）的異常粗大顆粒。
features: Two small-to-medium mononuclear leukocytes, lymphocyte-sized, with round nuclei and high N:C ratio
Coarse, dark purple-red cytoplasmic granules, most prominent in the lower cell and overlapping the nucleus
Upper cell shows fewer coarse granules in a thin rim of cytoplasm
Granules are larger and darker than normal azurophilic granules of large granular lymphocytes
Faded, pink-toned staining and limited resolution restrict assessment of chromatin and granule detail
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows two lymphocyte-sized mononuclear cells containing coarse, dark purple-red cytoplasmic granules, most conspicuous in the lower cell where granules surround and overlie the nucleus. The granules are larger and darker than normal azurophilic granules. Red cells are unremarkable. The staining is faded and resolution is limited, so granulocytes should be examined for similar inclusions. Findings are consistent with Alder-Reilly anomaly, which reflects accumulated mucopolysaccharide and should prompt evaluation for a mucopolysaccharidosis.

ddx.vs: Toxic granulation affects neutrophils in infection with fine-to-coarse granules accompanied by Dohle bodies and vacuoles, and is transient rather than involving lymphocytes.
Basophils have a segmented nucleus obscured by large, water-soluble dark blue-black granules, whereas these cells have round nuclei.
Chediak-Higashi shows fewer, giant fused granules in granulocytes and lymphocytes rather than many uniformly coarse granules.
LGLs have more abundant pale cytoplasm with a few fine azurophilic granules, not dense coarse dark granules.
